alerts.title: Rising creatinine on TDF during pregnancy
alerts.message: TDF is associated with renal toxicity including proximal tubular dysfunction and declining eGFR. Patient's creatinine rose from 0.8 to 1.1 mg/dL (38% increase) within 10 weeks of starting TDF/3TC/DTG, with eGFR now 78 mL/min/1.73m². Pregnancy normally increases GFR, so a creatinine rise is concerning and suggests TDF may be contributing. Against drug attribution: the absolute creatinine remains near normal range and phosphate is normal (3.8 mg/dL), arguing against significant proximal tubulopathy. However, the trend during pregnancy warrants close monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat creatinine and eGFR within 4 weeks. If creatinine continues to rise or eGFR falls below 60, consider switching TDF to TAF or alternative NRTI.

alerts.title: Pregnancy viral load monitoring frequency
alerts.message: Guidelines specify viral load monitoring every 3 months for pregnant and lactating women, compared to annually for non-pregnant adults. Patient initiated ART 10 weeks ago with current VL 89 copies/mL (suppressed from 125,000). The next VL should occur at approximately 6 months post-initiation per protocol, then every 3 months during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

evidence.recommended_action: Schedule next viral load at 6 months post-ART initiation, then every 3 months through pregnancy and breastfeeding period.

alerts.title: No clinician assessment or plan documented
alerts.message: No assessment or plan was documented for this visit. Given pregnancy, rising creatinine on TDF, and recent ART initiation, a documented plan should address renal monitoring, viral load scheduling, anaemia follow-up, and continuation of antenatal supplements. The patient's Hb of 10.8 g/dL indicates mild anaemia; ferrous sulfate and folic acid are already prescribed.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a comprehensive plan addressing renal monitoring, VL scheduling, anaemia management, and coordination with antenatal care.

evidence.recommended_action: Screen for TB at next visit (approximately 12 weeks on ART) and initiate TPT if eligible, per guideline recommendations.
